newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends sharply stronger after rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends sharply stronger after rate rise.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended more than half a U.S. cent stronger on Thursday at C$1.3815 (US$0.7238) from Wednesday's close of C$1.3935 (US$0.7176) after the Bank of Canada raised interest rates by 25 basis points, dealers said.
* The Bank of Canada raised the ceiling of its 50 basis point target range for Canada's overnight rate to 3.50 percent.
The central bank said in a statement after the move that the hike was designed to "counter excessive easing in monetary conditions and to provide support for the currency."
The Bank of Canada said last month that the need for further easing in monetary conditions had largely disappeared, implying it would like to see the dollar strengthen or rates rise.
"This (currency) move in the light of a 25 basis-point-hike has been incredibly dramatic. We've seen easings, we've seen tightenings, but they're usually not this violent," said a currency trader.
Analysts said the hike -- the first since February 1995 -- was likely the first of many and marked the end to a rate-cutting cycle that brought Canadians their lowest interest rates in decades.
The Bank of Canada intervened repeatedly on Thursday to buy Canada dollars as the currency weakened through key support at the C$1.3965 (US$0.7160) level.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 81.81 yen from Wednesday's close of 81.68 yen and rose to 1.2480 marks from 1.2362 marks.
